light:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity still CONCEPT image for Augurwell, a desktop physical tarot table. This is a new design exploration, not a screenshot of implemented functionality. Landscape 16:10 composition, refined digital art direction, restrained ethereal lightness and a slight occult/mathematical sensibility. The two input images are content references ONLY: existing Urban Tarot artwork The Star and The Sun. Keep their recognizable colorful urban illustrations, full opaque rectangular faces and white caption strips; do not replace them with generic moon/sun engravings or recolor them. Never recolor the card art to fit the environment.
Scene/state: one continuous grounded shallow 3D tabletop viewed from above at roughly 50 degrees, with three physical tarot cards resting nearly flat on the surface in a casually spaced triangle: Star face-up upper-left, selected Sun face-up slightly lower and central, one face-down card farther right. The Sun has the same physical dimensions as the other two, with just a very slight lift and a soft selection rim. No upright standing cards, no giant floating focus card. In the lower-left to lower-middle tabletop is the source deck: a shallow loosely overlapping fan of many thin physical card backs, enough to visibly convey a full deck, smaller in the composition than the three chosen cards. Card backs use delicate restrained silver geometric linework on opaque neutral material, no rich ornament.
Layout: very small AUGURWELL wordmark at upper left, a small quiet settings icon at upper right, abundant usable empty table space. Near the lower margin, one slim liquid-glass control dock containing clear Chinese words “牌义” and “重洗”, with the first gently emphasized. In the open right-side margin place only “The Sun”, one small line “Life, hope, and clarity”, and the action “展开牌义”, without a panel box or a second duplicate card preview. A small “已揭示 2 张” lives by the dock. No tabs for history or spreads, no journaling or question field. Keep useful text readable with stable contrast; avoid garbled decorative labels. No added fake percentages or predictions.
Materials and meaning: real paper cards remain opaque and legible; glass is limited to the compact control dock and a thin portion of the finite table edge. Soft contact shadows visibly ground every card. A short delicate sequence of two tiny light marks near the revealed cards can suggest information accumulating, but do not draw branches, star charts, orbital webs or causal connectors between freely placed cards. The table's outline is quiet and recoverable, not a huge ornamental glass ring. Calm stationary scene, no cosmic cloud/fog background, no particle showers, no gold filigree, no crystals, no fairy figures, no formula wall, no nested glass panels, no busy border.
This image is one of a paired material comparison; retain this same card state and physical gesture logic across versions.
LIGHT MATERIAL DIRECTION: moon-white and pale warm-gray open daylight, with a faint cool lavender/cyan reflected hue confined to glass thickness. The surface is an expansive matte pearl-gray plane, with a softly bounded thin translucent playing area, a restrained refractive edge and little soft shadows. Make the space feel open, airy, gently luminous and ethereal, while original colorful art carries most of the visual intensity. Clear charcoal interface type. Fluid glass feels thin, tactile and polished, with local curvature and modest rainbow separation only on its edge. No glossy mirrored floor, large glass ribbons, washed-out white text or broad glowing blobs.

refinement: Edit this Augurwell UI concept to remove the accidental still-life styling and make the usable card-table interface clean. REMOVE ALL plants, leaves, plant shadows, vases, stones, dishes, candles, candle holders, crystal/glass balls, cups and other nonfunctional physical props around the table. Fill those areas with a clean uninterrupted version of the existing neutral playing surface and quiet ambient light. Do not replace the removed objects with any other decorations. The only physical objects allowed are tarot cards and the thin playing surface. Move/scale ONLY the lower-left source fan enough that the entire fan fits within the viewport with a clear left and bottom margin, preserving a usable gap to the bottom controls. Retain the three placed cards, their current upright colorful Urban Tarot faces, white source captions, their approximate positions, the original light-or-dark tonal direction, restrained fine tabletop glass edge, and the readable text/control arrangement. Keep the selected card's highlight small and quiet. No new rings, stars, particles, fog, scenery, symbols, extra UI panels, new tabs or background furniture. This is a clean functional interface styleframe, not a staged product photograph. Keep the landscape format and all existing useful text.
